mainTopic: חזקיה's funeral honor, the reward for תורה and kindness, and the opening משנה on רגל
overview: This amud finishes the discussion of how חזקיה מלך יהודה was honored at his death. רבי יהודה says 36,000 men walked before him with bared shoulders. רבי נחמיה objects that אחאב got the same honor. He says instead that they laid a ספר תורה on the bier and said 'this man kept what is written in it.' The גמרא asks that we do this today too, and gives several answers. The last answer, from רבי יוחנן, is that only for חזקיה did they say 'he taught' the תורה. Next, רבי שמעון בן יוחאי teaches that whoever is busy with תורה and גמילות חסדים earns the portion of two tribes, יוסף and יששכר. Then the first פרק ends with a הדרן. The second פרק opens with a משנה: an animal walking normally and breaking things is רגל and pays full damage, while kicking, pebbles, a second broken vessel, and a chicken's string or hopping pay half.

steps.title: How long they learned at חזקיה's grave
steps.stepSummary: The dispute ends. One opinion says the learning at חזקיה's grave lasted seven days, and another version says thirty.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other one said: seven days. And some say: thirty days.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a list of opinions about how long people sat and learned at חזקיה's grave to honor him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An earlier opinion gave a shorter time. Here the second opinion says seven days. A different version of the tradition says thirty days. Everyone agrees on the kind of honor, which was a ישיבה at the grave. They only disagree about how long it lasted.

keyTerms.meaning: And some say it (a different version of the tradition)

phrases.english: And the other one said: seven.
phrases.notes: This is about how many days they sat and learned at חזקיה's grave, which the גמרא was just discussing.

phrases.english: And some say: thirty.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the dispute from the previous daf about how long the honor of learning at the grave lasted.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The second opinion says seven days of learning at the grave. Another version of that opinion says thirty.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: 36,000 mourners went before him
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא reads the פסוק differently. According to רבי יהודה, the honor was that 36,000 men with bared shoulders walked before חזקיה at his funeral.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: 'And they gave him honor in his death.' This is חזקיה king of יהודה, before whom 36,000 men went out with bared shoulders. These are the words of רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא with a new explanation of what the 'honor' in the פסוק was. רבי יהודה says it was a huge funeral procession.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before this, the honor was explained as learning at the grave. Here רבי יהודה says it was a visible act of mourning: 36,000 men walked in front of the bier with their shoulders uncovered.

keyTerms.meaning: The Rabbis taught (this opens a ברייתא)
And they gave him honor in his death
These are the words of רבי יהודה

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
"And they gave him honor in his death"
this is Hezekiah king of Judah,
before whom went out
thirty-six thousand men with bared shoulders,
these are the words of Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: וְכָבוֹד עָשׂוּ לוֹ בְמוֹתוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different explanation of the same פסוק, through a ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יהודה, the honor was 36,000 men walking before חזקיה with bared shoulders.

steps.title: רבי נחמיה: אחאב got the same honor
steps.stepSummary: רבי נחמיה challenges רבי יהודה. The wicked king אחאב had the same kind of procession, so it cannot be the special honor the פסוק means for חזקיה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי נחמיה said to him: But didn't they do the same thing for אחאב?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי נחמיה attacks רבי יהודה's explanation. If even a wicked king got this honor, it is nothing special.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק is praising חזקיה, so the honor must be something unique to a righteous king. A procession that אחאב also received is just normal royal honor. It cannot be what the פסוק is pointing to.

keyTerms.meaning: But didn't ... ? (a question that is really a challenge)
אחאב, the wicked king of ישראל

steps.confusionAlert: This is worded as a question, but it is really an attack: 'They did this for אחאב too, so your explanation doesn't work.'

phrases.english: Rabbi Nehemya said to him:
But didn't they do the same before Ahab!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי נְחֶמְיָה: וַהֲלֹא לִפְנֵי אַחְאָב עָשׂוּ כֵּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly challenges רבי יהודה's explanation.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהודה's claim that the 36,000 mourners were the honor in the פסוק
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The wicked אחאב received the same honor, so it is ordinary royal honor and not a special praise for חזקיה.

steps.title: רבי נחמיה: a ספר תורה was placed on his bier
steps.stepSummary: רבי נחמיה gives his own explanation. They placed a ספר תורה on חזקיה's bier and said, 'This man kept what is written in this.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, they placed a ספר תורה on his bier and said: This one fulfilled what is written in this.
steps.whatsHappening: After rejecting רבי יהודה's view, רבי נחמיה explains what the special honor really was. It was a ספר תורה laid on the bier.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This honor fits only a righteous king, which answers the problem raised about אחאב. It declared that חזקיה's life matched the תורה. So the honor was about his righteousness, not just the size of the crowd.

keyTerms.meaning: His bier (the bed the body is carried on)

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהודה says the honor was 36,000 mourners. רבי נחמיה rejects that because אחאב got it too. He says the true honor was a ספר תורה on the bier, declaring that חזקיה kept everything written in it.
steps.whyThisMatters: It teaches that the greatest honor for a person is not the size of the crowd at the funeral. It is being recognized as someone who lived by the תורה.

phrases.english: Rather, that they placed a Torah scroll
on his bier,
and they said: This one fulfilled
phrases.notes: 'This one' means חזקיה, and 'this' in the next line means the ספר תורה.

phrases.english: what is written in this.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא שֶׁהִנִּיחוּ סֵפֶר תּוֹרָה עַל מִטָּתוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the challenge in step 3, רבי נחמיה offers his own explanation in place of רבי יהודה's.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The honor in the פסוק was a ספר תורה laid on חזקיה's bier, with the declaration that he fulfilled what is written in it.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The unique honor was public recognition of חזקיה's faithfulness to the תורה, something a wicked king could never receive.

steps.title: But we do this nowadays too
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי נחמיה: we honor great scholars this way today, so what was special about חזקיה?
steps.simpleTranslation: But nowadays we also do this!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי נחמיה's explanation from step 4. If we still honor great scholars with a ספר תורה, then this cannot be the unique honor the פסוק describes for חזקיה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי נחמיה himself rejected רבי יהודה's view because אחאב got the same procession. Now his own explanation runs into the same problem: a 'special' honor cannot be something everyone gets.

phrases.english: But nowadays we also do this!
phrases.notes: 'This' means what was done for חזקיה: honoring a great Torah scholar's funeral with a ספר תורה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי נחמיה's explanation from step 4
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי נחמיה's claim that placing a ספר תורה on the bier was חזקיה's unique honor
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The honor the פסוק describes must be unique. This one is still given to scholars today, so it is not unique.

steps.title: We take it out but do not lay it down
steps.stepSummary: First answer: today we take the ספר תורה out, but we do not place it on the bier.
steps.simpleTranslation: We take it out, but we do not lay it down.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that today's honor is smaller. We bring out a ספר תורה, but only חזקיה had it actually placed on his bier.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer keeps רבי נחמיה's explanation by pointing to a detail. Laying the ספר תורה on the bier itself was the part that only חזקיה received.

keyTerms.meaning: We do not lay it down (on the bier)

phrases.english: We take it out,
but we do not lay it down.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 5
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the details of the practice
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Today's honor seemed the same as חזקיה's
steps.terutzMaskana: Today we only take the ספר תורה out. Only חזקיה had it placed on his bier.

steps.title: We lay it down but do not say 'he fulfilled'
steps.stepSummary: Second answer: even if we lay the ספר תורה down today, we do not say 'this one fulfilled what is written in this.'
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you want, say: we also lay it down, but we do not say 'he fulfilled.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers another answer. Even if we place the ספר תורה on the bier today, we do not announce that the person fulfilled what is written in it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This answer moves the unique part from the action to the words that were said. The statement 'this one fulfilled' was said only about חזקיה.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you want, say (introduces another answer)
He fulfilled (what is written in the תורה)

phrases.english: And if you want, say:
we also lay it down,
but we do not say 'he fulfilled.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second answer to the challenge of step 5
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing what is said, not what is done
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Laying the ספר תורה down today would make the honors identical
steps.terutzMaskana: The words 'this one fulfilled' were said only for חזקיה

steps.title: רבי יוחנן's care before answering
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר בר חנה describes how רבי יוחנן would not answer a question after leaving the bathroom until he washed, put on תפילין and made a ברכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר בר חנה said: I was walking with רבי יוחנן to ask about this teaching. When he went into the bathroom and I asked him something, he would not answer until he washed his hands, put on תפילין and made the ברכה.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup for the next step. רבה בר בר חנה tells a story about how he got רבי יוחנן's answer to our question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The story shows רבי יוחנן's great respect for Torah words. He would not say words of Torah until he had washed and put on his תפילין. His actual answer comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: A teaching or a Torah topic
He would not answer us (literally, would not resolve it for us)

phrases.english: רבה בר בר חנה said:
I was walking together with רבי יוחנן
to ask about a teaching.
When he would go into the bathroom
and I would ask him something,
he would not answer us
until he washed his hands
and put on תפילין and made the ברכה.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה: הֲוָה אָזֵילְנָא בַּהֲדֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sets up a third answer to the challenge of step 5
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוחנן did not speak words of Torah until he had washed, put on תפילין and made a ברכה

steps.title: We say 'he fulfilled' but never 'he taught'
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן's answer: today we even say 'he fulfilled,' but we do not say 'he taught.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Then he told us: We even say 'he fulfilled,' but we do not say 'he taught.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives his answer. Today we may even say 'this one fulfilled what is written in this,' but only for חזקיה did they say 'he taught' it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This answer gives up both earlier distinctions. Today we may lay the ספר תורה down and say 'he fulfilled.' What was unique to חזקיה was the praise that he taught the תורה.
steps.whatToRemember: The final answer about חזקיה: what made his honor unique was being praised for teaching the תורה, not only for keeping it.

phrases.english: And then he told us:
We even say 'he fulfilled';
we do not say 'he taught.'
phrases.notes: For חזקיה they said this man taught what is written in this ספר תורה. That praise is not said today.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives רבי יוחנן's answer, introduced by the story in step 8
steps.terutzResolutionType: Moving the unique element to a different praise
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Saying 'he fulfilled' today would make the honors the same
steps.terutzMaskana: Only חזקיה was praised with 'he taught'

steps.title: Isn't doing greater than learning?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: learning is called great because it leads to doing, so doing seems greater. Why is 'he taught' a higher praise than 'he fulfilled'?
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't the Master say: Learning תורה is great, because learning leads to doing?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי יוחנן's answer. A known teaching says learning is great because it leads to doing, which suggests doing is the higher level.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If learning is valued only because it brings a person to doing, then 'he fulfilled' should be the top praise. So why would 'he taught' be the higher, unique honor?

keyTerms.meaning: But didn't the Master say (introduces a known teaching used as a challenge)

phrases.english: But didn't the Master say:
Learning תורה is great,
because learning leads to doing!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי יוחנן's answer from step 9
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that 'he taught' is a higher praise than 'he fulfilled'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Learning is praised for leading to doing, so doing is greater. 'Fulfilled' should then be the top praise.

steps.title: Learning for yourself versus teaching others
steps.stepSummary: Answer: the teaching about doing being greater is about learning for yourself. Teaching others is higher.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult: this is about learning, and that is about teaching.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the two ideas talk about different things. Doing is greater than learning for yourself, but teaching others is greater still.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The teaching 'learning leads to doing' compares doing with one's own learning. Teaching others is a different level, so praising חזקיה for teaching is still the highest praise.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult (the two ideas do not clash)

steps.whatToRemember: Doing is greater than learning for yourself, but teaching תורה to others is a higher level still. That was חזקיה's unique praise.

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
this is about learning, that is about teaching.
phrases.notes: The Master's teaching is about learning for yourself. The praise of חזקיה is about teaching others.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא; הָא לְמִיגְמַר, הָא לְאַגְמוֹרֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 10
steps.terutzResolutionType: Two different cases (learning for yourself versus teaching others)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: All Torah study ranks below doing
steps.terutzMaskana: Only learning for yourself ranks below doing. Teaching others is higher.

steps.title: The reward for Torah and kindness
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן, in the name of רבי שמעון בן יוחאי, explains a פסוק: whoever is busy with תורה and גמילות חסדים merits the portion of two tribes.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said in the name of רבי שמעון בן יוחאי: What does the פסוק 'Happy are you who sow by all waters, who send out the feet of the ox and the donkey' mean? Whoever is busy with תורה and acts of kindness merits the portion of two tribes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new teaching. רבי שמעון בן יוחאי explains a פסוק to teach the reward for learning תורה and doing acts of kindness.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a new topic. The פסוק is read as a hint to תורה and גמילות חסדים, and the reward is the portion of two tribes.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the meaning of what is written

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחַאי,
phrases.english: רבי יוחנן said in the name of רבי שמעון בן יוחאי:
What is the meaning of what is written:
'Happy are you who sow by all waters,'
'who send out the feet of the ox and the donkey'?
Whoever is busy with תורה and acts of kindness
merits the portion of two tribes.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחַאי, מַאי דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new teaching that explains a פסוק
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Whoever is busy with תורה and גמילות חסדים merits the portion of two tribes

steps.title: Sowing means charity and water means Torah
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows from other פסוקים that 'sowing' in the פסוק means צדקה and 'water' means תורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it says, 'Happy are you who sow.' 'Sowing' always means charity, as it says, 'Sow for yourselves for charity, reap according to kindness.' And 'water' always means תורה, as it says, 'Ho, all who are thirsty, go to the water.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is proving where רבי יוחנן got his idea that the פסוק talks about תורה and kindness. It decodes two words of the פסוק using other פסוקים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 12 we were told that this פסוק is about someone busy with תורה and גמילות חסדים. Here the גמרא backs that up: 'sowing' links to צדקה and kindness through a פסוק in הושע, and 'water' links to תורה through a פסוק in ישעיהו. So 'those who sow by all waters' are people who do kindness and learn תורה.

keyTerms.meaning: Happy are you, fortunate are you
This word means only... (a way of decoding a word in a פסוק)

phrases.english: As it is stated: 'Happy are you who sow'
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 32:20. The full פסוק goes on: 'by all waters, who send out the feet of the ox and the donkey.'

phrases.english: and 'sowing' means only charity,
as it is stated: 'Sow for yourselves for charity,
reap according to kindness';
and 'water' means only Torah,
as it is stated: 'Ho, all who are thirsty, go to the water.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source and word meanings behind רבי יוחנן's statement in step 12.
steps.raayaObject: That the פסוק is about people busy with תורה and kindness
steps.raayaSupportSource: הושע 10:12 for sowing = צדקה; ישעיהו 55:1 for water = תורה

steps.title: The portion of two tribes: יוסף and יששכר
steps.stepSummary: The 'portion of two tribes' comes from the ox and donkey in the פסוק: the ox stands for יוסף, who gets a canopy, and the donkey stands for יששכר.
steps.simpleTranslation: And 'he merits the portion of two tribes': he merits a canopy like יוסף, as it says, 'יוסף is a fruitful vine, its branches run over the wall.' And he merits the portion of יששכר, as it says, 'יששכר is a strong-boned donkey.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the second half of רבי יוחנן's teaching, the reward of 'two tribes.' It reads the ox and donkey in the פסוק as hints to יוסף and יששכר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The end of the פסוק mentions 'the ox and the donkey.' יששכר is directly called a donkey, and יוסף is pictured as an ox elsewhere. So the reward is a share like each of these two tribes: an honor canopy like יוסף and the portion of יששכר.

phrases.english: And 'he merits the portion of two tribes' —
he merits a canopy like Joseph,
phrases.notes: This is the 'ox' in our פסוק, since יוסף is compared to an ox (דברים 33:17).

phrases.english: as it is written: 'Joseph is a fruitful vine,
its branches run over the wall';
phrases.notes: בראשית 49:22. The branches spreading over the wall are the picture of a canopy.

phrases.english: and he merits the portion of Issachar,
as it is written: 'Issachar is a strong-boned donkey.'
phrases.notes: בראשית 49:14. This is the 'donkey' in our פסוק.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After decoding 'sowing' and 'water,' the גמרא now decodes 'the ox and the donkey' to explain the reward.
steps.raayaObject: That the reward is the portion of two tribes
steps.raayaSupportSource: בראשית 49:22 for יוסף's canopy; בראשית 49:14 for יששכר as a donkey

steps.title: A second explanation of the two tribes' reward
steps.stepSummary: Some say the reward is different: enemies fall before him like יוסף, and he gains understanding like יששכר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say: his enemies fall before him like יוסף, as it says, 'With them he shall gore the nations together, to the ends of the earth.' And he merits understanding like יששכר, as it says, 'And of the children of יששכר, men who understood the times, to know what ישראל should do.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another opinion about what exactly the 'two tribes' reward is. The idea of יוסף and יששכר stays the same, but the blessings are different.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both opinions agree the ox is יוסף and the donkey is יששכר. They differ only on which blessing of each tribe he receives. Here it is יוסף's strength over enemies (the goring ox) and יששכר's wisdom in knowing what ישראל should do.

keyTerms.meaning: He will gore (like an ox with its horns)

steps.whatToRemember: Whoever is busy with תורה and kindness gets the reward of two tribes: יוסף (canopy, or victory over enemies) and יששכר (his portion, or deep understanding).

phrases.english: Some say:
his enemies fall before him like Joseph —
as it is written: 'With them he shall gore the nations
together, to the ends of the earth';
phrases.notes: דברים 33:17. 'With them' means with the ox's horns.

phrases.english: and he merits understanding like Issachar —
as it is written: 'And of the children of Issachar, men who understood the times,
to know what Israel should do.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different reading of the same reward explained in step 14.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The two tribes' reward is victory over enemies like יוסף and understanding like יששכר.

steps.title: הדרן — Closing the chapter of ארבעה אבות
steps.stepSummary: The first פרק of בבא קמא, ארבעה אבות, is finished.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, ארבעה אבות.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the standard closing line said when finishing a פרק. It is not part of the discussion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: הדרן means 'we will return to you,' a way of showing love for the learning and a hope to learn it again. The next line on the daf starts the new פרק.

keyTerms.meaning: We will return to you (said at the end of a פרק)
The four main categories of damage, the name of the first פרק

phrases.english: We will return to you, 'Four Main Categories'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the פרק after the aggadic ending.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The first פרק of בבא קמא, ארבעה אבות, is complete.

steps.title: What it means that the foot is forewarned
steps.stepSummary: The משנה defines רגל: an animal is considered מועדת to break things in the normal course of walking.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: In what way is the foot forewarned? It breaks things as it walks. An animal is forewarned to walk in its normal way and break things.
steps.whatsHappening: The new פרק opens with a משנה that explains the אב נזיקין of רגל: an animal breaks things just by walking normally.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Walking is normal animal behavior, so the owner is always treated as warned, which makes it מועדת. That means he pays נזק שלם for anything broken this way. The cases that follow are measured against this basic picture.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Foot': damage an animal causes while walking normally
Forewarned: the owner is fully responsible and pays full damage

steps.whyThisMatters: Every case in this משנה is judged by asking whether it fits this basic definition of normal walking.

phrases.english: MISHNA: In what way is the foot forewarned?
To break things in the course of its walking.
The animal is forewarned to walk in its usual way and break things.
phrases.notes: So the owner pays full damage for this kind of breaking.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the new פרק after the previous פרק ended in Step 16.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An animal breaking things while walking normally is רגל and is מועדת, so the owner pays נזק שלם.

steps.title: Kicking and flying pebbles pay half damage
steps.stepSummary: If the animal kicked, or pebbles shot out from under its feet and broke vessels, the owner pays only חצי נזק.
steps.simpleTranslation: If it was kicking, or pebbles were shooting out from under its feet, and it broke vessels, he pays half damage.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives two cases close to walking that still pay only חצי נזק: kicking, and damage from צרורות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Kicking is not normal walking. It is unusual behavior, so it does not get the full payment of רגל. Pebbles are different: the walking is normal, but the damage comes from something the foot sent flying, not from the foot itself. This case also pays only half.

keyTerms.meaning: Pebbles kicked up by an animal's feet
Half the cost of the damage

steps.confusionAlert: Pebbles fly up during completely normal walking, yet the payment is still only half. Don't assume that anything happening while walking counts as full רגל.

phrases.english: If it was kicking,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ שֶׁהָיוּ צְרוֹרוֹת מְנַתְּזִין מִתַּחַת רַגְלֶיהָ –
phrases.english: or pebbles were shooting out from under its feet –

phrases.aramaic: וְשָׁבְרָה אֶת הַכֵּלִים, מְשַׁלֵּם חֲצִי נֶזֶק.
phrases.english: and it broke the vessels, he pays half damage.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָיְתָה מְבַעֶטֶת, אוֹ שֶׁהָיוּ צְרוֹרוֹת מְנַתְּזִין מִתַּחַת רַגְלֶיהָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sets limits on the basic rule of Step 17 by giving cases that pay less than full damage.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Kicking and damage from pebbles pay חצי נזק.

steps.title: One vessel broken, then a second broken by its fall
steps.stepSummary: If the animal stepped on a vessel and broke it, and that vessel fell and broke another, the owner pays full damage for the first and half damage for the second.
steps.simpleTranslation: If it stepped on a vessel and broke it, and it fell on another vessel and broke it, he pays full damage for the first and half damage for the second.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a two-part case. The first vessel was broken directly by the foot, and the second was broken by the falling first vessel.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first vessel is classic רגל, so the owner pays נזק שלם. The second vessel was not touched by the foot. It was hit by something the foot set in motion, just like pebbles, so it gets the חצי נזק rule of צרורות. One event can produce two different payments.

phrases.english: If it stepped on the vessel and broke it,
and it fell on a vessel and broke it –
phrases.notes: 'It' is the first vessel, the one the animal stepped on, falling onto a second vessel.

phrases.english: for the first he pays full damage,
and for the last he pays half damage.

steps.triggerLanguage: דָּרְסָה עַל הַכְּלִי וּשְׁבָרַתּוּ, וְנָפַל עַל כְּלִי וּשְׁבָרוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Combines the full-damage rule of Step 17 with the half-damage rule for indirect damage from Step 18.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Direct breaking by the foot pays נזק שלם. A second vessel broken by the falling first vessel pays חצי נזק.

steps.title: Chickens walking normally pay full damage
steps.stepSummary: Chickens are מועדין to walk normally and break things, so their owner pays full damage.
steps.simpleTranslation: Chickens are forewarned to walk in their usual way and break things.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה applies the basic רגל rule to chickens: if they break things just by walking normally, it is full רגל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule is not limited to large animals. Whatever an animal does while walking in its normal way counts as רגל and is מועדת. This sets up the next step, where unusual chicken behavior pays less.

phrases.english: Chickens are forewarned to walk in their usual way and break things.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the basic definition of Step 17 to chickens.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Chickens breaking things by walking normally are רגל and pay נזק שלם.

steps.title: Chickens with a string on their leg or hopping pay half
steps.stepSummary: If a string tied to a chicken's leg broke something, or the chicken was hopping and broke vessels, the owner pays חצי נזק.
steps.simpleTranslation: If there was a string tied to its legs, or it was hopping and breaking vessels, he pays half damage.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives two chicken cases that fall short of normal walking, so they pay only חצי נזק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A string on the leg means the damage came from something attached to the chicken, not from the foot itself. Hopping is not the chicken's normal way of walking. Neither case is plain רגל, so the payment is half.
steps.whatToRemember: The basic rule: normal walking that breaks things directly is רגל and pays נזק שלם. Kicking, pebbles, a second vessel hit by a falling one, a string on a chicken's leg, and hopping all pay חצי נזק.

phrases.english: If there was a string tied to its legs,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ שֶׁהָיָה מְהַדֵּס וּמְשַׁבֵּר אֶת הַכֵּלִים –
phrases.english: or it was hopping and breaking the vessels –
he pays half damage.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָיָה דְּלִיל קָשׁוּר בְּרַגְלָיו, אוֹ שֶׁהָיָה מְהַדֵּס
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the chicken rule of Step 20 with unusual cases that pay half.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Damage from a string tied to a chicken's leg, or from a hopping chicken, pays חצי נזק.
